name: Ounjougou early ceramic vessels
description: Fired-clay vessels at Ravin de la Mouche document an early West African pottery tradition.

impact.note: Fired vessels were a new ability here and later West African and Saharan pottery plausibly followed, though descent from this one site is unproven.

date.label: Before 9400 calibrated BCE
date.basis: Stratigraphic terminus ante quem, not an invention date.

events.statement: A bowl fragment and other ceramic sherds were redeposited in fluvial unit HA1 at Ravin de la Mouche before 9400 cal BCE, as bounded by the overlying dated deposits.

evidence.locator: pp. 909–911, HA1 formation and assemblage; Figs. 1 and 3
evidence.supports: The sherds are reworked material in stratified unit HA1. The overlying dated deposits give a terminus ante quem for redeposition.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest inspected attestation for this local case.

caveats: The deposits date the redeposition of the sherds. Cooking wild cereals is a hypothesis based on environmental and functional comparisons. Their contents and the route by which pottery spread remain unresolved.

unresolved.note: Regional invention and diffusion hypotheses require comparison; no origin or carrier is established here.
HA1 phytoliths are too sparse to establish local vegetation for that unit. The better grass phytolith record from adjacent units cannot identify the contents of HA1 pots.

research.note: Independent review checked the 2020 publication, especially p. 7: its 9400 cal BCE terminus ante quem applies to the oldest sherds at Ravin de la Mouche, not all Ounjougou finds; vessel function and diffusion remain uncertain.
